tb21_profile.skill: Compile an exhaustively correct rule system (full chess move generation with castling, en passant, promotion and check legality) into a restricted computational substrate - an ordered list of re.sub rewrite rules - which means both knowing the rules and reasoning about what a one-pass regex rewrite chain can encode
tb21_profile.domain: Python `re` semantics (alternation order, backreferences, capture-group replacements, single-pass substitution), chess rules and FEN encoding, program generation
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec, at the deep end: emit a data artefact (JSON of regex/replacement pairs) that is itself a program, under size budgets, verified against held-out positions

TMax-15K.reason: Decode a DSL, then implement its state machine and expression evaluator exactly: the same build-a-rule-engine-from-a-written-spec work as chess move generation.
Explicitly 'regex alone is insufficient': implement a character-by-character state machine and survive an adversarial corpus. Directly about regex expressive limits.
Reverse-engineer a stack language and write an exact interpreter for it; same must-be-exhaustively-correct semantics reproduction.
Implement an emulator for a custom instruction set recovered from a spec image; every opcode must be right or the tests fail.
Parse a build DSL and interpret it, tracking variables and evaluating expressions; small-language semantics implemented from prose.
Write a Bash interpreter for a build-configuration DSL - implementing a language in a substrate that is a bad fit for it, like regex here.
Reimplement a C math interpreter safely in Rust with identical behaviour; exact-semantics reimplementation under a new substrate.
Strict grammar validator in C for arithmetic expressions; enforces a formal language precisely, the sub-skill regex-chess needs for FEN fields.
Character-by-character state-machine parser in C, explicitly forbidden from using heavy regex; teaches when a scanner beats a pattern.
Port a state-machine parser from Python 2 to 3 and finish an unimplemented function; only state-machine familiarity transfers.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Author one regex using a backreference to force a consistent separator and emit the captures as JSON; real regex construction, at toy scale.
Use rgxg to generate several regular expressions and validate a log with them; generating regexes programmatically is the core regex-chess move.
Export a single backreference-bearing regex as a module; regex-authoring practice, no state encoding.
Same phone-number backreference regex family, with the spec hidden in the filesystem; regex correctness under a discovered contract.
Duplicate-family backreference regex validation task; only single-pattern authoring transfers.
Another phone-regex variant in the same family; listed because RTS offers nothing deeper on regex.
Static-analysis workflow over a Brainfuck interpreter; forces reading an interpreter loop, adjacent to compiling into a restricted substrate.
Drive a custom Lisp interpreter to solve for an unknown value; exercises reading a small-language evaluator, not writing one.
Write an EQL query script against a dataset; authoring a program in a restricted declarative language, but no rewriting semantics.
Use a supplied Lisp interpreter on a data file to compute a value; near-zero transfer beyond running an interpreter.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Generate several regular expressions with rgxg and reproduce their exact output; regex construction rather than regex use. Packet says FREE, verifier_strength.json says strong - unresolved, so per_source only.
Write one regular expression that classifies four email strings correctly; pattern-correctness-under-test, trivially small.
Static analysis of a C Brainfuck interpreter; requires understanding an instruction dispatch loop, adjacent to encoding computation in a minimal substrate.
Emulate keygen logic with radare2 ESIL: run a computation in a substrate not designed for it, which is the regex-chess trick in miniature.
Implement N-Queens: exhaustive legal-placement generation with board-attack geometry, the same combinatorial-completeness demand.
Solve a constraint puzzle in Prolog; expressing a rule system declaratively instead of imperatively.
Step a Sudoku solver under a debugger; board-state reasoning, no rule implementation of your own.
Extract a field with a regular expression; only pattern authoring, one line of it.
Regex extraction of Hangul character runs versus individual characters; teaches character-class precision, nothing structural.
Write a minimal command interpreter shell in C; a tiny language loop, weakly related. TerminalWorld has nothing on chess or regex-as-computation.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: The bug is operator ordering inside a lexer regex alternation - exactly the ordered-alternatives hazard that decides whether a regex rewrite chain is correct.
Another Pygments lexer regex fix; lexer rule sets are ordered pattern lists, the same structure as re.json.
PEG parser internals in parsimonious; grammar-rule ordering and matching semantics are the parent skill of regex rule chains.
TextFSM is literally a state machine driven by an ordered list of regex rules - the closest architectural analogue in SWE-Smith.
Same regex-driven state-machine engine; fixing it means reasoning about rule order and state transitions.
Grammar-expression evaluation bug in a PEG library; transfers reasoning about how a rule set consumes input.
Parser-combinator semantics in pyparsing; same family of ordered-alternative matching pitfalls.
Tokenizer/parser internals for Python source; grammar-level correctness, distant from chess rules.
Markdown parsing driven by regex rule tables; inline-rule ordering bugs resemble substitution-order bugs.
Boyer-Moore string-search index bug; exact string-matching algorithm correctness, no rewriting or rule generation.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Lark grammar/parser caching bug; requires understanding how a compiled grammar is serialised and replayed, the parser-generation mindset.
URL routing rule matching in Werkzeug - an ordered rule set converted to regexes, with precedence bugs of the same shape.
Another Werkzeug routing/converter issue; regex-backed rule compilation and matching order.
Hypothesis's from_regex strategy: generating strings that satisfy a regex forces reasoning about what a pattern actually accepts.
Property-based-testing internals; exhaustive-case thinking is what regex-chess needs for held-out positions.
Linter rules expressed as regexes over YAML/Jinja; rule-set maintenance, shallow.
Source-classification via lexing rules; pattern-driven categorisation, no state rewriting.
Black's source transformation; a rewriting system over syntax trees rather than strings, weak but real analogy.
Version-specifier grammar and regex parsing in packaging; precise pattern semantics over a small formal language.
Qiskit transpiler pass ordering; rule pipelines whose order changes the result, otherwise unrelated.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Minimum-bit chess game encoder: to index a move you must enumerate the legal moves in each position, so full move generation is the crux.
Capture groups and build replacement strings with re.sub backreferences - the exact API the re.json pairs are written in.
Chess engine with move generation, evaluation and search; chess-rule domain, though it leans on python-chess rather than implementing the rules.
Explains why /.*/g replaces twice: zero-length-match advancement, precisely the semantics that makes a substitution chain misbehave.
Fixes broken backreference syntax in an re.sub replacement string; the single most common failure mode when hand-writing rewrite pairs.
Replace a family of numbered tags with one pattern instead of enumerating variants; the generalise-don't-enumerate pressure the 100k-pair budget imposes.
Split at positions preceding uppercase runs, which needs zero-width lookaround; positional-assertion practice.
Keep separators when splitting by regex, i.e. control exactly what a pattern consumes versus preserves - the same accounting a rewrite rule needs.
Return match positions as well as matched text in JavaScript; teaches match-object mechanics, shallow.
N-Queens optimisation on an NxN chessboard: board-attack geometry and exhaustive search, but the task is performance tuning.

CalibForge.reason: The same artefact: a JSON list of [regex, replacement] pairs applied in a loop that must evaluate postfix Boolean expressions, under a pattern-count and size budget.
Implement a regex engine with Regex/Match classes; forces exact knowledge of what alternation, groups and anchoring do.
Write regex.c from a header's syntax contract, validated by a hidden suite; pattern-semantics mastery plus held-out testing, like re.json's unseen positions.
Implement match_pattern in C supporting ., *, +, character classes; backtracking-matcher semantics learned from the inside.
Brainfuck-to-C transpiler: compile a program from one computational substrate into another, emitting code rather than running it.
Walk a PGN game tree from a given FEN and aggregate every move played from that position; FEN handling plus per-position move enumeration.
Rush Hour solver over a 36-character board string: generate all legal piece moves from a packed string state and search - move generation on a string encoding.
Fix a script that reads FENs and emits best moves via Stockfish; FEN parsing and chess tooling, but the fix is plumbing.
Simulate Game of Life patterns from RLE files and classify them; deterministic rule application over a grid, exhaustively checked.
Debug a Connect Four engine that misjudges wins, draws and invalid moves; game-rule correctness with every case pinned.

final_top10.reason: Same artefact and same loop: a JSON list of [regex, replacement] pairs that must evaluate postfix Boolean expressions under a pattern-count and byte budget.
Minimum-bit chess encoder: indexing a move requires enumerating the legal moves in each position, so correct move generation is the crux.
Implement regex.c from a syntax contract and pass a hidden suite; pattern semantics from the inside, judged on held-out cases.
Build a regex engine with Regex/Match classes, which forces exact knowledge of alternation order, grouping and anchoring.
Capture groups and construct replacement strings with re.sub backreferences - the precise API every entry of re.json is written in.
Brainfuck-to-C transpiler: emit a program in a second substrate rather than execute one, the same compile-into-a-restricted-target move.
Operator ordering inside a lexer regex alternation - exactly the ordered-alternative hazard that decides whether a rewrite chain is correct.
Rush Hour solver over a packed 36-character board string: enumerate all legal moves from a string-encoded position and search.
Decode a DSL and implement its state machine and expression evaluator exactly; build-a-rule-engine-from-written-spec with no partial credit.
The task states regex alone is insufficient and demands a hand-rolled state machine that survives an adversarial corpus; teaches where patterns stop.

notes: CalibForge is decisive here: it contains a direct sibling of the TB2.1 task (software-engineering_20260420_020307_021, the same [regex, replacement] JSON program template, strong verifier) plus three regex-engine implementations. Nothing in the v1 pool came close on the regex-as-computation axis. Terminal-Lego also genuinely beats the v1 corpora: it is the only corpus with real chess tasks (task_14927, task_13538) and a cluster of substantive re.sub/backreference tasks; its weakness is depth, not relevance. TMax has no chess and no regex-as-computation - `search tmax "chess|FEN"` returns zero and its 328 regex hits are all log-parsing boilerplate - so its entries are interpreter/state-machine analogues. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis cannot field 10 defensible candidates; RTS's only regex content is one duplicated phone-number-backreference family, and TerminalWorld's is two one-line validation tasks. Watch out for two false-positive classes in the merge: (1) CalibForge filler tasks whose text names the TB2.1 task's domain while doing something unrelated - software-engineering_20260612_191200_021 says it 'evaluates ... for the regex-chess domain' but is a directory-hashing inspector; (2) the enormous 'write to /app/result.txt' overlap that put GCD and set-operation chores at the top of the RTS and TerminalWorld shortlists.
